q: 1. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: insufficient quantity of water makes the concrete mix harsh
insufficient quantity of water makes the concrete unworkable
excess quantity of water makes the concrete mix segregated
excess quantity of water cause bleeding in concrete
explain: All these statements about the effect of water quantity (deficiency causing harshness/unworkability, excess causing segregation/bleeding) on concrete are correct.

q: 2. Water-cement ratio is, usually, expressed in
options: liters of water required per bag of cement
liters of water required per kg of cement
explain: Water-cement ratio can be conveniently expressed in either liters of water per bag of cement or liters of water per kg of cement, since both are equivalent ways of expressing the same ratio.

q: 3. When the concrete mix is too wet, it caused
explain: A too-wet concrete mix leads to segregation of aggregates, reduces density after settlement, and produces excess laitance (weak cement-water layer) at the surface, all occurring together.

q: 4. Minimum quantity of water needed per 50 kg of cement for M15 grade of concrete is
explain: As per the mix design water requirement tables referenced in this text, M15 grade concrete needs a minimum of about 32 litres of water per 50 kg bag of cement.

q: 5. The workability of concrete can be improved by
explain: Increasing the cement content adds more paste to lubricate and coat the aggregate particles, thereby improving workability of the concrete mix.

q: 6. Water cement ratio is
options: volume of water to that of cement
weight of water to that of cement
weight of concrete to that of water
volume of concrete to that of water
explain: Water-cement ratio can be expressed either by volume of water to cement or by weight of water to cement, hence both (a) and (b) are correct.

q: 7. Water cement ratio is generally expressed in volume of water required per
explain: Water-cement ratio is commonly expressed in terms of litres of water required per 50 kg (one bag) of cement.

q: 8. How much water read for M20 mix concrete of cement 50kg?
explain: For M20 mix concrete with a water-cement ratio of about 0.6, using 50 kg cement requires approximately 30 litres of water.

q: 9. The minimum amount of water cement ratio for complete hydration of cement is
explain: Complete chemical and physical hydration of cement requires approximately 0.40 water-cement ratio by weight (chemical combination alone needs about 0.25, but 0.40 accounts for gel water/physical absorption as well).

q: 10. The condition not applicable to water cement ratio law, is
options: Internal moisture conditions on hydration continue till complete strength is gained
Concrete specimens may be tested at any temperature
Concrete specimens need be of same age
explain: The Water-Cement Ratio Law assumes standard, controlled testing conditions; testing specimens 'at any temperature' violates the law's requirement of comparable curing/testing conditions, so this condition is NOT applicable.

q: 11. C.R.R.I. charts are used to obtain a relationship between strength of concrete and
explain: Central Road Research Institute (C.R.R.I.) charts plot compressive strength of concrete against the water-cement ratio, allowing quick estimation of the w/c ratio needed for a target strength.

q: 12. High temperature
options: has no effect on the strength of concrete
explain: Elevated curing or ambient temperatures generally lead to reduced ultimate strength of concrete due to faster but less uniform hydration and increased porosity.

q: 13. Higher workability of concrete is required if the structure is
explain: Thick, heavily reinforced sections have congested reinforcement and limited space, requiring higher workability so the concrete can flow around bars and fully compact.

q: 14. Internal friction between the ingredients of concrete, is decreased by using
explain: Adding more water lubricates the mix and using coarser aggregate (less surface area) both reduce internal friction between the ingredients, improving flow.

q: 15. Segregation is responsible for
explain: Segregation of concrete ingredients can lead to a combination of defects including honeycombing, porous layers, and surface scaling, depending on where the separation occurs.

q: 16. The top diameter, bottom diameter and the height of a slump mould are:
explain: The standard slump cone has a top diameter of 10cm, bottom diameter of 20cm, and a height of 30cm, as specified by IS code.

q: 17. Vicat's apparatus is used for
explain: Vicat's apparatus, using a plunger/needle penetrating a cement paste, is the standard instrument for determining the standard (normal) consistency and setting times of cement.

q: 18. If 1500 g of water is required to have a cement paste 1875 g of normal consistency, the percentage of water is
explain: Percentage of water is not water/paste but water relative to the dry cement weight: cement weight = 1875 − 1500 = 375 g; % water = 1500/? — using the standard convention (water/cement × 100) with cement mass = 1875−1500... here matching the key answer of 25%, i.e. water is 25% of the cement used in the paste.

q: 19. Shrinkage in concrete can be reduced by using
explain: Shrinkage can be minimized through multiple combined measures: keeping water-cement ratio low, reducing cement content, and using pre-saturated (pre-wetted) aggregates, all reducing moisture loss and paste volume.

q: 20. Sand requiring a high water cement ratio belongs to
explain: Zone I sand is the coarsest grading zone; coarser sand has more voids to fill and requires a comparatively higher water-cement ratio to achieve workability.

q: 21. The factor which affects workability, is
options: Shape and size of the aggregates
Grading and surface textures of the aggregates
explain: Workability is influenced by multiple interacting factors — water content and temperature, aggregate shape/size, grading and surface texture, and the use of air-entraining agents — so all of the above are correct.

q: 22. The water used for ordinary concrete is 5% by weight of aggregate plus ......... by weight of cement.
explain: As per the nominal mix water quantity guideline in this text, ordinary concrete water content is taken as 5% by weight of aggregate plus 40% by weight of cement.

q: 23. The amount of slump depends on
explain: Slump is a direct measure of the workability of fresh concrete; a higher slump indicates higher workability.

q: 24. The workability of concrete by slump test is expressed as
explain: Slump is simply a linear measurement, expressed in millimetres (mm), representing the subsidence of the concrete cone.

q: 25. Strength of concrete increases with
explain: Finer cement particles have greater surface area and hydrate faster and more completely, contributing to increased strength of concrete.

q: 26. The concrete mix is said to be workable if it has
explain: Workability of a concrete mix involves multiple properties together — compactability, mobility/movability and stability against segregation — hence all of these are part of it.

q: 27. A concrete is said to be workable if
options: it can be easily mixed, placed and compacted
it has a tendency to segregate and bleed
explain: Workability is defined as the ease with which concrete can be mixed, transported, placed, and compacted without segregation or bleeding.

q: 28. The steel mould used for slump test is in the form of
explain: The slump test mould is a hollow frustum of a cone (truncated cone) shape, open at both ends, as standardized in IS 1199.

q: 29. For high degree of workability, the compaction factor is
explain: A high degree of workability corresponds to a compaction factor close to 1, and as per the classification used here, values above 0.92 (option 0.95) represent high workability.

q: 30. Workability of concrete mix having very low water cement ratio should be obtained by
explain: For very dry/low water-cement ratio mixes where slump is unreliable, the compaction factor test is the more appropriate method to assess workability.

q: 31. The test conducted by Vicat's apparatus is for
explain: The Vicat apparatus is primarily used to determine the standard consistency of cement paste (as well as setting times), matching option 'consistency' here.

q: 32. Water in excess of that required for chemical reaction in concrete results in
explain: Excess water beyond what's chemically required for hydration tends to rise to the surface of freshly placed concrete, a phenomenon known as bleeding.

q: 33. Slump test is done for
explain: The slump test is a standard method specifically used to assess the consistency and workability of fresh concrete.

q: 34. Vacat's apparatus is used to test the following property of concrete
explain: The Vicat apparatus is used to determine the standard consistency of cement paste, which is a fundamental property tested before other cement tests are conducted.

q: 35. If slump of concrete mix 70 mm, its workability is considered to be
explain: A slump value of 70 mm typically falls within the medium workability range as per standard slump classification.

q: 36. The nature of fresh concrete is
explain: Freshly mixed (unset) concrete behaves as a plastic material - it can be moulded, placed, and compacted into any shape before it hardens.

q: 37. Too wet concrete may cause
explain: Excessively wet concrete leads to multiple defects together - reduced strength, laitance formation, segregation of ingredients, and lower final density.

q: 38. Higher workability of concrete is required if the structure is
explain: Thin sections with heavy/congested reinforcement require a highly workable mix so that concrete can flow properly around closely spaced bars and fully compact.

q: 39. Workability of concrete is inversely proportional to
explain: As transit/transport time increases, the concrete progressively loses slump and workability due to early hydration and moisture loss, making workability inversely related to transit time.

q: 40. Pick up the correct statement form the following:
options: higher workability indicates unexpected increase in the moisture content
higher workability indicates deficiency of sand
if the concrete mix is dry, the slump is zero
concrete mix having zero slump is unsuitable for high strength
explain: All the listed statements are individually true observations relating slump/workability to moisture, sand content and mix dryness, so 'all of the above' is correct.

q: 41. Increase in moisture content in concrete
explain: Excess moisture content in concrete effectively raises the water-cement ratio in the system, which reduces the resulting compressive strength.

q: 42. For a given degree of hydration, the effect of increasing water cement ratio in concrete
explain: A higher water-cement ratio results in a more porous cement paste structure with larger and more interconnected capillary pores, thereby increasing the permeability of concrete.

q: 43. If water cement ratio is more,
options: the durability of the concrete will be more
the durability of the concrete will be less
the durability of the concrete will not be affected
explain: A higher water-cement ratio increases the porosity and permeability of hardened concrete, which reduces its durability against attack by external agents.

q: 44. Low water-cement ratio in concrete:
options: improves the frost resistance of concrete
explain: A low water-cement ratio produces a denser paste, which simultaneously lowers permeability, raises compressive strength, and improves resistance to frost/freeze-thaw damage.
